en.title: Longest Adjacent Identical Halves with Replaceable Question Marks
en.description:
You are given a string of lowercase letters and question marks; each question mark can be independently replaced with any lowercase letter. Find the maximum even length of a contiguous substring whose first and second halves are identical; the two halves must be adjacent.

This site independently prepared the standard I/O and the solution; bounds supplemented where the source lacks them and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the specification.
en.input: A single line containing the string. The original gives no length bound; this site adds 0≤length≤5000, with characters a..z or ?. Output 0 for an empty string or when no non-empty valid substring exists.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 4; 0; 0. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Enumerate the half-length h from large to small and scan the pairs of characters h apart, checking whether they are equal or include a question mark; h consecutive compatible pairs give the answer 2h.
